card.statement:
Let $\fing=\mf{sl}_2$, $k\ne -2$. Set $b(z)=\sqrt{2}b_1(z)=-\sqrt{2}b_2(z)$, so that $[b_{\lam}b]=\lam$. Then the right-hand-side of the formula in Corollary <<ref:Co:duality>> becomes

\begin{align*}
& :(\alpha_0\partial_z+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}b(z))(\alpha_0\partial_z-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}b(z)):
\&=\alpha_0^2\partial_z^2-L(z),
\end{align*}

where

$$L(z)=\frac{1}{2}:b(z)^2:+\frac{\alpha_0 }{\sqrt{2}}\partial_z b(z).
$$

It is well-known and is straightforward to check that the field generates the Virasoro algebra of central charge $1-6(k+1)^2/(k+2)$. Thus $\W^k(\mf{sl}_2)$, $k\ne -2$, is isomorphic to the universal Virasoro vertex algebra of central charge $1-6(k+1)^2/(k+2)$.
card.label: Example 85
